item.title: When do the Lions get to Germany? Dan Campbell details travel plans
item.description: The Detroit Lions are all business as they prepare for an overseas flight to Munich, Germany, for an international game with the New England Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 15. Lions coach Dan Campbell relayed the team's plans for the trip, including how they'll deal with practice, when they'll make the flight, and how they'll handle the acclimation process upon arrival, during his weekly radio interview with Costa & Jansen with Heather on 97.1 The Ticket. Campbell said the travel is "not going to" impact the team as they look to make it five straight wins against the reigning AFC champion. "We're gonna practice our tails off [Wednesday] and Thursday. We're gonna take a shower. We're gonna jump on this freaking plane. We're gonna take a nap, and then we're going to wake up, we're going to meet, and we're going to walk-through red-zone practice," Campbell said. "We're gonna stay up for another four or five hours later than normal. We're gonna wake up, go full speed for about 45 minutes the day before the game. They're going to walk around a little bit, enjoy the sights, get a good sleep. We're going to wake up and be ready to play. "And then we're going to jump on the plane, get ready for Tampa (Bay in Week 11), and be ready for that game, too. Then we're going to be ready for the Chicago Bears, Thanksgiving, at our place. We're gonna be ready to go." More: Detroit Lions trade deadline tracker: Latest news, updates More: Lions finalize trade to land safety Andre Cisco from Jets The Patriots (5-4) will be highly motivated coming off a devastating 45-27 home loss to the Green Bay Packers. New England has had an up-and-down season since last year's Super Bowl appearance, but Campbell expects coach Mike Vrabel to have his guys ready for the trip in a game the Patriots need to win after losing two of their last three. Campbell said the Patriots' performance against Green Bay "is not a good snapshot of what New England is." "This team plays hard, man. It's a talented unit," Campbell said. nbianchi@detroitnews.com @nolanbianchi This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: When do the Lions get to Germany? Dan Campbell details travel plans

item.title: ‘I will be number one P4P’: David Benavidez focused for Cieslak challenge
item.description: David Benavidez says that becoming undisputed champ at cruiserweight is “inevitable,” as he prepares to face Michal Cieslak with three title belts on the line on December 5 at home in Arizona. But Benavidez doesn’t want to limit the vision to just becoming an undisputed champion. He’s also looking to be seen as the world’s best boxer, bar none. “I got two belts in my first fight at cruiserweight and now I’m going for a third,” Benavidez said. “Me being undisputed is inevitable. I’m going to make my way to the top of the pound-for-pound list very soon. I will be number one.” Benavidez (32-0, 26 KO) dominated Gilberto “Zurdo” Ramirez to win the WBA and WBO cruiserweight titles on May 2 in Las Vegas, and will be trying to add the WBC belt currently held by Cieslak (28-2, 22 KO), who comes over from Poland as a heavy underdog. “The biggest challenge with Cieslak is that he’s coming into this fight defending his title for the first time,” Benavidez said. “Every fighter has that motivation after winning the title that you really don’t wanna let it go. He’s gonna come in strong, but I don’t run away from any competition.”

item.title: McIlroy’s Take On Recent DQ Shows Rules Must Change
item.description: Jeff Curry-Imagn Images Rory McIlroy labeled Frank Kennedy’s disqualification from Q-School as “harsh” but backed the need for stricter behavior rules. The 21-year-old Manchester native lost his chance at a DP World Tour card after swinging a putter in anger on the 11th hole. GolfMagic reported that officials deemed the outburst as “serious misconduct” following the incident at the Infinitum Resort in Spain. Kennedy missed a birdie putt and damaged the green while walking to the next hole. The Incident and the Reaction Kennedy’s actions sparked immediate debate across the tour. American golf journalist Ryan French first broke the news that Kennedy and his father begged rules officials to review the decision. The young golfer released a statement late Monday claiming he did not understand why the penalty was so severe. “I have always respected and followed the Rules of Golf,” he said. Kennedy added that many senior players he spoke to were surprised by the ruling. He noted, “If accidental contact like this, repaired at once, is a disqualification offence, I will respect that.” McIlroy addressed the situation while preparing for the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai. He told reporters that the situation seemed very unfortunate. The Northern Irishman discussed the incident with his caddie Harry Diamond out on the course. McIlroy stated, “It seems harsh but at the same time, I think it’s good that golf and the authorities are cracking down on things like this.” He called it an “unbelievably unfortunate incident” but supported the crackdown on misconduct. A New Era of Discipline Governing bodies for the four men’s majors have agreed to clamp down on bad behavior. This shift follows several high-profile incidents during this year’s major championships. At Augusta National, Sergio Garcia drove his club into the tee box and a water cooler. Scotland’s Robert MacIntyre directed a middle finger at the 15th green after a quadruple-bogey. Both players received reprimands for their actions. Jon Rahm also faced a warning for tossing his club at the Open at Royal Birkdale. He briefly “forgot” about the new code of conduct, the Spaniard confessed. Joaquin Niemann earned the distinction of being the first player penalized with shot deductions for this mid-round. These events show that the era of ignoring player temper tantrums is over. The rules are now enforced with zero tolerance. Kennedy’s case is a clear warning to every player on tour. The governing bodies want to protect the image of the sport. They will not tolerate outbursts that damage the course or disrespect the game. Why the Strict Stance Matters Kennedy’s loss of a tour card is a heavy price for a single moment of anger. The penalty removes a highly-rated youngster from the path to professional golf. Yet the message sent to the field is clear and necessary. Golf needs to stop excusing bad behavior because of talent. The sport suffered too much negative attention from past incidents. item.title: Kyle Hamilton joins kids from Boys & Girls Club for football and learning
item.description: Kyle Hamilton’s latest community appearance connected his childhood experience with an opportunity to support Baltimore youth. The Ravens safety and Team Toyota athlete joined elementary school teacher Mary Crippen, creator of NFeLementary, for an afternoon of football-themed learning and games at the Baltimore Ravens Boys & Girls Club. Both grew up participating in Boys & Girls Clubs, giving the event a personal connection beyond their shared interest in football. The gathering took place Monday during Baltimore’s extended break between games. Toyota brought Hamilton and Crippen together to connect with local club members through activities designed to make learning engaging and accessible. Kyle Hamilton shares a connection with club members The program paired NFL-themed games and trivia with the Boys & Girls Clubs of Metro Baltimore’s emphasis on academic success, healthy lifestyles, and leadership development. Hamilton brought the perspective of an NFL player who once attended a club himself. Crippen brought her experience using football to engage elementary school students through NFeLementary, combining her work in education with the sport’s ability to capture children’s attention. Their backgrounds gave the gathering a connection to the opportunities Boys & Girls Clubs provide. For Hamilton, participating meant returning to an organization that shaped his upbringing while spending time with children in the community where he now plays. The activities offered another way to connect football with learning, using the game as an entry point for participation and curiosity. Bringing an athlete and an educator together also connected two different approaches to encouraging young people. Ravens touchdowns support Baltimore youth programs The event was part of Toyota’s broader community involvement surrounding football. Toyota, the NFL’s official automotive partner, also supports local youth through the Ravens Toyota Community Touchdowns Program. Under that initiative, Baltimore-area Toyota dealers will donate $414 to the Boys & Girls Clubs of Metro Baltimore for every Ravens touchdown scored this season, according to the event materials. Those contributions support the organization’s work with local children. Hamilton’s appearance added a personal element to that partnership. Alongside Crippen, he returned as a former club member, with an opportunity to contribute to the next generation's experience. item.title: Mercedes And Williams Tie For Ninth Constructors’ Title In 2026
item.description: Michael C. Johnson-Imagn Images Mercedes has secured its ninth Constructors’ Championship, tying the record set by Williams. This achievement places the German manufacturer alongside the British team in the history books, behind only Ferrari and McLaren. Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali led the tributes to the team for this major milestone on the track. The win marks a return to the top for Mercedes after a period of struggle. Kimi Antonelli’s record as the youngest ever Drivers’ World Champion coincides with this same season, according to Formula1.com . Winning both titles makes 2026 a historic year for the sport and the Mercedes team. Toto Wolff Joins a Legend The championship victory puts team principal Toto Wolff in rare company. According to Formula 1 Official, his ninth title as a leader draws him level with Sir Frank Williams. Wolff stands alongside Frank in the record books. Domenicali praised the team effort required to reach this point. He stated, “My huge congratulations to everyone at the Mercedes Formula 1 Team on becoming 2026 Constructors’ World Champions. Reaching the summit of Formula 1 is never the achievement of one person alone.” The CEO emphasized that the result came from hundreds of people working together at the factory and the circuit. Every member of the team should feel proud of what they have accomplished this season. Rivals Celebrate Hamilton’s Milestone While the team celebrated, Lewis Hamilton reached a personal milestone with his 400th race start. Fernando Alonso, a rival driver, offered his respects to the veteran on the grid. Alonso noted that Hamilton has had an incredible career in F1, with all 400 races in a very competitive position. Alonso added, “But yes, Lewis obviously has had an incredible career in F1, and 400 races, all of them in a very competitive position. Congratulations to him, and hopefully a good race and a good weekend for him.” The 400 Club is a group that few drivers ever enter. New champion Kimi Antonelli could join that same club as early as 2041. At 24 races a year, the young Italian has a long path ahead if he stays healthy and fast. A New Chapter for the Sport Only Ferrari has more wins with 16, and McLaren sits second with 10. Williams and Mercedes now share the third spot with 9 titles each. Mercedes previously won the title for eight consecutive seasons from 2014 to 2021. The 2026 win breaks a recent run where McLaren claimed the 2024 and 2025 titles. A Mercedes-powered car has secured the championship for the third year in a row. Domenicali concluded the official remarks by noting the significance of the moment. He said, “Mercedes have returned to the very top, and in doing so have written another remarkable chapter in the history of Formula 1.” The wait for another Constructors’ Championship ended last weekend in Sao Paulo.

item.title: Agent confirms Liverpool star is in talks over new deal
item.description: Agent confirms Liverpool star is in talks over new deal Alisson Becker Contract Talks Give Liverpool a Clear Goalkeeping Decision Liverpool have a decision to make on Alisson Becker, and it looks like the process has already started. Early discussions are underway over a new deal for the Brazilian, whose current contract is due to expire next June. That matters, because Alisson remains one of the few players in this squad who can still decide games on his own. Liverpool know it, Alisson knows it, and now his camp have effectively confirmed it in public. Alisson Becker open to Liverpool stay There has been noise around several Liverpool contracts in recent months, including Alexis Mac Allister, but Alisson’s situation is simpler. He wants to stay. His agent, Ze Maria, made that clear, saying to WinWin : “Alisson loves Liverpool very much. We are in preliminary talks to renew the contract.” That is not a deal done, and it is not even close to one yet. Still, when a player is happy, the agent is talking and the club are engaged, it usually means there is something concrete to discuss. Photo: IMAGO Liverpool contract talks hinge on age and value The issue is not quality. Alisson has delivered that for years. The issue is age and cost. He is 34, and Liverpool have not built a reputation for handing major renewals to players in that bracket. Then again, rules in football tend to bend for elite players. Liverpool already made one such call when they renewed Mohamed Salah’s deal in April 2025. Alisson could fall into the same category, particularly if the club believe there is still another season or two of top-level performance there. His current wages are reported at £250,000 per week, which already places him among the top earners in the squad. Any extension would involve another serious financial commitment. That is the real calculation here. Crystal Palace display showed Alisson quality Recent mistakes had raised a few questions, fairly enough, but his display against Crystal Palace was a reminder of why Liverpool have trusted him for so long. He made a series of high-level saves and looked like himself again, calm, sharp and decisive. That is why this conversation is happening. If Alisson were declining badly, there would be no serious debate. Instead, Liverpool are weighing cost against certainty, and in his position certainty carries a premium. Nothing is settled yet. These are early talks. But the signs are positive, and for Liverpool, keeping Alisson Becker may still be the most sensible piece of business available.

item.title: Spain manager’s advice to Lamine Yamal as he backs him to follow in Messi, Ronaldo’s footsteps
item.description: Spain manager’s advice to Lamine Yamal as he backs him to follow in Messi, Ronaldo’s footsteps The Spanish national team have already assembled for the ongoing international break, and Barcelona stars including Joan Garcia, Pedri and Pau Cubarsi have already assembled in Luis de La Fuente’s camp. The big name, Lamine Yamal, has not joined up with some niggling pain in his knee and has been exempted from the team’s first game. He has, however, been called up and is expected to be back for the game against England. It will be a special international break this time around, as it marks the first time both Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo will not be in action after both players announced their international retirements. In that sense, the spotlight will not shine a little bit brighter on the next generation of stars, and Lamine Yamal is one who will hog a major part of that spotlight. De La Fuente’s advice Lamine backed to mark an era in football. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Speaking to the media at a press conference, Spain NT manager Luis de La Fuente was asked if he saw Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe capable of filling the void left by Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo’s retirements. “They are going to mark an era in football, for sure,” he began, as quoted by Mundo Deportivo . “It is very good for football that there is not only one star who is the reference for everyone,” he added. Speaking on the importance of competition between two top stars, the manager said, “There must be two or three players who are references and who believe in that spirit of joy, of follow-up and what sport is a bit: rivalry, always healthy.” Advice to Lamine Yamal De La Fuente had special advice for Yamal. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The coach was then asked what advice he would give to the player who is under his tutelage – Lamine Yamal. “He is a very mature boy for his age, but he needs us to accompany him, like any boy his age who is still training. He is aware,” he began. “In private, he shows you that maturity that I am saying, but outside of that environment you also have to protect yourself and defend yourself from everything around you,” he added. De La Fuente then praised Yamal for how he soaks up pressure and criticism with maturity, saying, “And he does it very well. I admire him because a 19-year-old boy, who endures the media pressure he has endured since he was 16, is not easy. It’s very difficult.” “And he does it with tremendous naturalness. You have to tell him to keep growing, improving and working as he does. This way he will have all the doors open to be a legendary footballer,” he added.

item.title: Official | Vincent Kompany returns to work at Bayern Munich
item.description: Official | Vincent Kompany returns to work at Bayern Munich Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany has taken another significant step towards returning to the touchline following his recent health scare. The Bundesliga champions confirmed on Tuesday that the 40-year-old Belgian has returned to the club’s Säbener Straße training facility. Kompany has been absent from his coaching duties since collapsing while observing a training session involving Bayern’s reserve team on October 23. He was subsequently hospitalised, with further medical examinations reportedly revealing an irritation of the meninges. Bayern have now confirmed that their head coach is recovering and has been back at the club’s training facilities since the beginning of the week. Kompany is also undergoing rehabilitation for a shoulder injury. According to the Münchener Tageszeitung , the Belgian was back working at his office computer by approximately 10 a.m. on Tuesday morning. Vincent Kompany could return after international break Bayern have not yet confirmed when Kompany will resume his responsibilities on the touchline. However, honorary president Uli Hoeneß suggested during an appearance on Bayerischer Rundfunk’s Sonntags-Stammtisch that the coach could return following the November international break. This would potentially put Kompany in contention to oversee Bayern’s Bundesliga encounter with 1. FC Cologne on November 20. In Kompany’s absence, assistant coach Aaron Danks has overseen first-team affairs, with Bayern winning all five competitive fixtures during that period. GGFN | Peter Weis

As Ovechkin prepares for retirement, other teams have celebrated him , giving gifts to the Great 8 as he visits their city one final time. Regardless of the outcome of this season, the greatest goal scorer of all time will be heading to Toronto for induction into the Hockey Hall of Fame at some point down the road. The biggest question is: when will it happen? Traditionally, players have to wait three years to be eligible, but there is the possibility that the Hall of Fame could waive the waiting period , something Pierre LeBrun of The Athletic explored. “And Alex Ovechkin? He has announced this will be his final NHL season, and some have wondered if the Hockey Hall of Fame should waive its three-year waiting period for the all-time NHL goals leader, as it did for players like Gordie Howe, Mario Lemieux and Wayne Gretzky,” LeBrun wrote. item.title: Tom Brady calls out what current NFL players are ‘really missing’ compared to his generation
item.description: L.E. Baskow/Las Vegas Review-Journal/Tribune News Service via Getty Images NFL legend Tom Brady has suggested that modern athletes are ‘really missing’ someone to challenge them every day to be their best. Brady was selected in the sixth round of the 2000 NFL draft by the New England Patriots, perhaps suggesting at the time that he would not go on to become one of the best players in history. However, he worked hard throughout his career to cement his legacy. But he has now questioned ‘Who’s challenging’ the new generation of players to be their very best. In a video shared on X/Twitter , he said: “We would play in any weather and we were challenged every day to be our best, too. And I think that’s maybe what the modern athletes [are] really missing. “Who’s challenging those kids to be their very best? Not who’s paying for their lunch money that day or who’s paying for the sponsorship. “It’s like who’s making that person a better, more complete athlete, at the end of every game. And that’s what I appreciate about coaching and organisations that push our players to be better.” Brady is one of the most decorated players in the history of the sport and holds the record for the most Super Bowl wins (7). After an initial retirement in 2022, he confirmed in February 2023 that his NFL career was over for good. item.title: Winter is Coming, But Hope Remains
item.description: 79 Years of Solitude – by Mario Crescibene Part 1 Part 2 Part 3 Part 4 Part 5 Part 6 Resting in the hammock of my rooftop apartment in Medellín, I can’t think of anything to write about. As the hammock sways back and forth and the sun sets on the Aburrá Valley, I think back on a season that had held so much potential… and not just for the Guardians. item.description: Grêmio aim to clear injury list and keep momentum against the bottom four After securing a place in the Copa do Brasil final and enjoying three days off, Grêmio's squad returns to training this Wednesday (11). item.title: Bickerstaff Makes His Stance on Cade Cunningham Clear
item.description: Detroit Pistons superstar guard Cade Cunningham was on the floor for only 26:31 against the Washington Wizards on Monday night. He picked up his fifth personal foul in the third quarter and did not return until midway through the fourth , finishing with 17 points on 43.8 percent shooting from the field in a 122-111 win for Detroit. Head coach J.B. Bickerstaff was asked what Cunningham does so well, in comments reported by Hunter Patterson of The Athletic . Bickerstaff said, “He just needs to be himself. Cade has been amazing since we’ve been here at understanding the moment and doing what’s right in the moment. He’s always put the team first, so this isn’t going to be about him doing something for him. It’s going to be what the game deems necessary and how (defenses) decide to defend him.” Nov 8, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Pistons guard Cade Cunningham (2) drives past Los Angeles Lakers forward Jake LaRavia (12) in the first half at Little Caesars Arena. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Cade Cunningham shaped the Pistons win in other ways Even with the 17 points, Cunningham grabbed three rebounds, recorded seven assists and added one steal. He is about making the right play for his teammates and getting them involved. Cunningham is averaging 22.3 points and 7.6 assists per game this season, and that assist average ranks ninth in the NBA . The number is down from the 9.9 assists per game he posted last season, but Cunningham is still willing to share the basketball with his teammates. Detroit has needed that playmaking more than usual. Center Jalen Duren, who has been out since late October, will miss at least two more weeks with a right hamstring strain, the Pistons said Sunday, and that latest Duren update leaves Cunningham setting up a reshuffled frontcourt. Three Pistons outscored Cunningham against Washington Duncan Robinson and Daniss Jenkins each scored 22 points in the game for Detroit, and Jenkins added eight assists. As for John Collins, he led the Pistons with 24 points and 10 rebounds against the Wizards. Detroit needed all of it. Washington’s Anthony Davis went for 44 points and 13 rebounds and the Pistons still pulled away. It was good to see other players on this team be able to contribute and help out Cunningham. item.description: Jaguars make Brian Thomas Jr. trade decision after major Monday deals originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Jacksonville Jaguars are the NFL's biggest spender at this year's NFL trade deadline. While the Chicago Bears have spent two first-round picks already, the Jaguars have made the most moves of note so far. All on Monday before deadline day, James Gladstone acquired Jessie Bates III, Davon Godchaux, and Jordan Davis to get some massive upgrades on the defensive side of the ball. Now, the focus shifts to wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. and if he's traded or not. According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , the Jaguars have made their decision: Thomas is staying put. Jacksonville has told NFL teams as much, with Thomas now set to remain with the Jaguars as they pursue a Super Bowl title. Jaguars plan to keep Brian Thomas Jr. despite trade speculation "The Jaguars plan to keep Brian Thomas Jr. through the trade deadline, per sources," Fowler reports. "They have relayed that to interested teams." While there was bound to be plenty of interest in Thomas from teams like the Kansas City Chiefs and the San Francisco 49ers , the Jaguars are electing to keep Thomas this season. After adding Jordan Davis in a trade with the Philadelphia Eagles and Jessie Bates III in a trade with the Atlanta Falcons , deciding to keep Thomas through the trade deadline is a sensible decision for the Jaguars. They're all-in, and Thomas should help in some way. It's not a major surprise, especially considering that the Jaguars are trying to win it all this year, and trading Thomas to a potential playoff opponent wouldn't make sense. MORE : Jaguars reportedly acquiring Falcons' Pro Bowl safety in major trade Besides, if the Jaguars were to lose Parker Washington or Jakobi Meyers to injury, not having Thomas at their disposal would be a major blow. Even though Thomas might be third on the depth chart at best, with Josh Cameron and Travis Hunter also being involved, the Jaguars are better off keeping him in hopes Thomas can provide any value down the stretch for their Super Bowl push. The trade value for Thomas was also likely not good enough to convince the Jaguars to move him, as it might've been hard for the Jaguars to get a second-round pick for Thomas, and a third-rounder might not have been a lock either. For a Super Bowl contender, keeping a WR like Thomas is a perfectly reasonable decision to make. While WR-needy teams might've wished they had moved Thomas, for the Jaguars, keeping him is the right call for the 2026 season. item.description: Victor Wembanyama now shares a wild NBA record with Stephen Curry originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Victor Wembanyama scored 40 points in 25 minutes during the San Antonio Spurs ’ 122-96 win over the Phoenix Suns on Monday. It was his fifth career game with at least 40 points in fewer than 30 minutes, tying Curry for the most in NBA history, according to Real App. The 25-minute performance was as efficient as it was brief. Wembanyama went 15-for-19 from the field, made two of his three 3-point attempts and added 11 rebounds and nine blocks. San Antonio built a commanding lead, allowing the 7-foot-4 center to sit for much of the fourth quarter. Five games, two very different paths Curry built his reputation as one of basketball’s most explosive scorers, capable of turning a few minutes into a game-changing run. Wembanyama’s route to the same mark looks different: he can pile up points while also changing what opponents dare to do near the basket. Victor Wembanyama ties Steph Curry for the most games ever with 40+ PTS in under 30 MIN. https://t.co/ebSqgy4T8i — Real App (@realapp) November 10, 2026 That combination was on display against Phoenix. Wembanyama scored from the perimeter and around the rim, then swatted away nine shots. He didn’t need a late-game scoring push to reach 40; the Spurs’ lead was already secure before the final minutes. The outing also extended a remarkable stretch. Four games earlier, Wembanyama put up career highs of 52 points and 24 rebounds, along with eight blocks, in a narrow win over Dallas. He has made a habit of reaching huge scoring totals without needing a heavy workload. MORE : Celtics receive alarming Paul George warning as NBA scout suggests 60-game limit The record fits a historic start A 40-point game is rare on its own. Doing it in fewer than 30 minutes takes an unusual mix of scoring pace and efficiency, and often means a player either catches fire quickly or has done so much damage that the fourth quarter becomes unnecessary. Wembanyama has now done it five times, matching Curry’s mark. The record is another eye-catching entry on a résumé that already includes the 52-point, 24-rebound Dallas performance and two games with at least 40 points, 10 rebounds and eight blocks in his last four outings. The Spurs are winning, Wembanyama is putting up numbers that barely fit on a scoreboard, and now he shares a record with one of the greatest scorers of his generation. It’s a remarkable combination, and a reminder that Wembanyama’s ceiling is still hard to measure. item.title: Fangio, Haywood deadline third batch of Sebring's 75 all-time greatest drivers
item.description: Motorsport photo Juan Manuel Fangio, one of Formula 1's most iconic World Champions and a two-time winner at Sebring, and multi-time Sebring winner Hurley Haywood have been selected as part of the third "Class of 75" driver group. This elite list recognizes the most successful drivers in the history of the 12 Hours of Sebring, and it is being revealed in five batches of 15 leading up to the historic 75th anniversary running of the race on March 20, 2027. The 75 drivers were chosen by a 10-person panel of sports car racing experts and divided into randomly selected lists of 15. Joining Fangio and Haywood in this third release are: Frank Biela German driver Frank Biela started nine races at Sebring International Raceway, all of them with Audi, and in most cases, at race end his teams were either celebrating in victory lane or contemplating a close defeat. Biela recorded four overall wins (2000, 2003, 2004) between 1999 and 2007 and backed up those wins with second-place finishes in 2001 and 2005. Audi won the Mobil 1 Twelve Hours of Sebring each year from 2000 through 2007, Biela’s last year of competition at Sebring. Vic Elford Although Englishman Vic Elford, known as 'Quick Vic' to many fans, had greater accomplishments at other circuits, he left an indelible mark on Sebring as well with an overall victory in 1971 and a second-place overall finish in his first start in 1968. With only five Sebring starts, the long-time Porsche works driver was a contender in all five events, although in 1970 he failed to finish when the car was involved in an accident on lap 61, and engine failure put him out in his final race at Sebring in 1972. Juan Manuel Fangio Fangio was one of the most famous drivers to take part in the 12 Hours of Sebring in the 1950s, and although he only competed in three races (1954, 1956, 1957) the five-time world champion Argentine driver captured two 12-Hour overall titles – 1956 in a Scuderia Ferraria 860 Monza and 1957 in a Maserati 450S. His only other entry, in 1954, resulted in a disappointing DNF after only 51 laps in a Scuderia Lancia D-24. Ron Fellows The name Ron Fellows was synonymous with both Corvette and consistency in the Mobil 1 Twelve Hours of Sebring from 1999 through his final race in 2008. The Canadian scored four GT victories in the American muscle car – each time with Johnny O’Connell – and he also set the pole-winning speed twice. His victories came in 2002, 2003, 2004 and 2008. He finished on the podium in eight of 11 races and finished inside the top 10 overall eight times and as high as fourth overall in 2004. His only race not in a Corvette – his first – was in 1998 when he drove a Porsche 911.
